svg.title: A Nested Annual Enterprise Sales Cohort
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-enterprise-opportunity-funnel; chart type: funnel; title: A Nested Annual Enterprise Sales Cohort; subtitle: 100 target accounts narrow to seven collected customer contracts.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative mature-year cohort, not an observed conversion benchmark. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Seven contracts averaging $200,000 in gross license and service billings produce the $1,400,000 Base-Case revenue. Assume delivery, billing, and collection occur within the modeled year.; caption: Track conversion and elapsed days separately: the canonical time to first deal is 3–12 months, so these annual results are not a first-month sales commitment.; stages: label: Target accounts; value: 100 named enterprise accounts with channel fit; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Create a deduplicated account cohort with a compatible software estate, supported geography, identifiable buyer, and documented renewal or deployment trigger.; label: Qualified discovery; value: 40 accounts; 40% of the initial cohort; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Confirm a reachable procurement owner, real purchasing timeline, vendor eligibility, and a problem that can be solved within the pod's delivery capacity.; label: Validated opportunities; value: 20 accounts; 50% of qualified discovery; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Verify license quantities, budget ownership, technical fit, and the applicable deal-registration position before investing in detailed solution design.; label: Executable proposals; value: 10 accounts; 50% of validated opportunities; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Issue customer-specific quotes or private offers with confirmed vendor pricing, purchasing route, implementation scope, acceptance terms, and collection exposure.; label: Collected contracts; value: 7 accounts; 70% of executable proposals; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Seven times $200,000 equals $1,400,000 in gross annual resale and service billings. Vendor acquisition costs remain expenses rather than additional revenue.

text.title: A Nested Annual Enterprise Sales Cohort
text.tspan: A Nested Annual Enterprise Sales Cohort

circle.title: label: Target accounts; value: 100 named enterprise accounts with channel fit; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Create a deduplicated account cohort with a compatible software estate, supported geography, identifiable buyer, and documented renewal or deployment trigger.

label: Qualified discovery; value: 40 accounts; 40% of the initial cohort; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Confirm a reachable procurement owner, real purchasing timeline, vendor eligibility, and a problem that can be solved within the pod's delivery capacity.

label: Validated opportunities; value: 20 accounts; 50% of qualified discovery; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Verify license quantities, budget ownership, technical fit, and the applicable deal-registration position before investing in detailed solution design.

label: Executable proposals; value: 10 accounts; 50% of validated opportunities; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Issue customer-specific quotes or private offers with confirmed vendor pricing, purchasing route, implementation scope, acceptance terms, and collection exposure.

label: Collected contracts; value: 7 accounts; 70% of executable proposals; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Seven times $200,000 equals $1,400,000 in gross annual resale and service billings. Vendor acquisition costs remain expenses rather than additional revenue.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative mature-year cohort, not an observed conversion benchmark. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Seven contracts averaging $200,000 in gross license and service billings produce the $1,400,000 Base-Case revenue. Assume delivery, billing, and collection occur within the modeled year.
